correction.text: Montenegro without 'the Bay of Kotor', annexed 'as part of the Italian Governorate of Dalmatia', and without Plav and Gusinje ('a significant amount of the Andrijevica district including Plav and Gusinje') and 'the town of Ulcinj', lost to Albania; the page adds 'some villages around Tutin and Rožaje' to the occupied core

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, Cliopatria has no Montenegro shape for 1914-2005. The page gives no area (page silent), only 'By 31 July 1941, the population of the occupied territory was estimated at 411,000'; the spec is Montenegro less the Kotor bay municipalities, Plav and Ulcinj (about 11,400 km2). The same sentence of the page also has Montenegro lose to Albania 'a strip of land north of Lake Scutari' and 'an area northeast of Podgorica', and begins 'Montenegro lost Metohija to Albania, including Bar'; the gazetteer has no unit for the strip or the area and the Bar clause is unclear, so they stay in the shape (Ulcinj subtracted by the eu-21-x reviewer, 2026-11-01). The page says 'Western and central Kosovo were also annexed to Albania' and that the territory included 'some villages around Tutin and Rožaje' (Serbian Sandžak), which the shape does not carry. The same land stayed in the shape under German occupation from 12 September 1943 to December 1944.

ledger.note: 18 April 1941: Italy occupies Montenegro. Infobox 'Italian occupation: 18 April 1941'; 'The Italians moved through on 16 April on their way to Dalmatia'; on 17 April the XVII Corps commander got authority 'to set up a new government in Cetinje'; the lead calls it 'an occupied territory under military government'.
18 April 1941: Italian military government of Montenegro begins. Infobox 'Italian occupation: 18 April 1941'.

12 July 1941: independence is declared and a restored Kingdom of Montenegro is proclaimed under an Italian regent. 'The declaration was passed by acclamation on 12 July'; the page speaks of 'the proclamation on the previous day of a restored Kingdom of Montenegro headed by an Italian regent', so 11 or 12 July. On 13 July 1941 'there was a general uprising against the Italians, initiated by the Montenegrin branch of the KPJ'; infobox 'Independence canceled: 24 July 1941'.
3 October 1941: the occupied territory is retitled the Governorate of Montenegro. Infobox 'Governorate established: 3 October 1941'; Pirzio Biroli, governor from 23 July 1941 on the page's table.

region.text: Montenegro, left by the Italians after the armistice

ledger.note: September 1943: Italian rule ends. 'On 3 September 1943 (but not made public until the 8th), the Italians concluded an armistice with the Allies'; Barbasetti di Prun's term ends 10 September 1943.

region.text: the former Italian governorate under Nazi German occupation

ledger.note: 12 September 1943: Germany occupies Montenegro. Infobox 'German occupation: 12 September 1943'; 'The territory of the former Italian governorate of Montenegro was placed under Nazi German occupation'; Axis occupation page: 'The former Italian kingdoms of Albania and of Montenegro were placed under German occupation'.

wars.name: 13 July uprising

zones.text: Montenegro without 'the Bay of Kotor', annexed 'as part of the Italian Governorate of Dalmatia', and without Plav and Gusinje ('a significant amount of the Andrijevica district including Plav and Gusinje') and 'the town of Ulcinj', lost to Albania; the page adds 'some villages around Tutin and Rožaje' to the occupied core

wars.outcome: A general uprising against the Italians, 'initiated by the Montenegrin branch of the KPJ', begins on 13 July 1941 and ends the puppet Kingdom of Montenegro (independence cancelled 24 July 1941); the page does not say how long the insurgents held ground.
wars.note: The 13 July Uprising article itself was not opened (page budget). No rebel dossier: no extent and no duration of rebel-held land on the pages.

certainty.note: The pages name what was cut off (the Bay of Kotor to Dalmatia, western and central Kosovo and the Plav-Gusinje area to Albania) but give no lines; the Sandžak edge (Tutin, Rožaje) is not located.

sources.title: Italian governorate of Montenegro
sources.note: Identity, 18 April 1941, 12 July 1941 declaration, 13 July uprising, 24 July cancellation, 3 October 1941 governorate, governors, 12 September 1943 German occupation, December 1944 withdrawal, 411,000 people (31 July 1941). No area figure.

sources.title: Axis occupation of Yugoslavia
sources.note: Italy 'gained control over Montenegro'; German occupation of the former Italian Montenegro after 8 September 1943; Partisans liberated Risan and Podgorica between October and December 1944.

notes: Cliopatria's Montenegro row (eu-18 montenegro dossier) has shapes only to 1915 and from 2006; this dossier fills 1941-1944 only, and 1919-1940 (Montenegro inside Yugoslavia) and 1945-2005 need nothing separate (they are part of Yugoslavia). The pages do not give: an area, the dates of the Bay of Kotor and Plav annexations, the extent or duration of the rebel hold of July 1941 (no contest events were written), the Partisan liberation of Cetinje or Podgorica day. Pirzio Biroli's start is 23 July 1941 in the table but the page also says he was appointed after 3 October 1941. The two renames (12 July and 3 October 1941) carry the puppet Kingdom and the governorate; the Kingdom of Montenegro was never drawn as territory beyond the occupied core. Region names the gazetteer lacks: none (the municipality names resolve).
